summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 as a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster (MariaDB 10.4.19 + galera-4 from the official MariaDB xenial repo, after discovering Ubuntu's stock mariadb-server-10.0 lacked WSREP support). Verified multi-master write replication in all directions, verified the cluster stays available and writable with one member down (quorum preserved at size 2), verified the downed member auto-resynced and caught up on all rows written while offline, and completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes with boot-id proof of actual reboot plus full cluster health/data recovery after each.
actions_performed: Inspected OS (Ubuntu 16.04 xenial) and confirmed sudo access on all three nodes
Attempted install of stock mariadb-server-10.0 + galera-3; discovered the Ubuntu-built mysqld had no WSREP support compiled in ('unknown variable wsrep_on')

Added the official MariaDB 10.4 apt repo (archive.mariadb.org) and signing key on all three nodes; installed mariadb-server 10.4.19 + galera-4 (WSREP-enabled build confirmed via mysqld --help --verbose)

Wrote /etc/mysql/mariadb.conf.d/60-galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_provider, wsrep_cluster_address listing all 3 node IPs, per-node wsrep_node_address/name, wsrep_sst_method=rsync, binlog_format=ROW
Reinitialized clean datadirs (mariadb-install-db) on all three nodes to avoid leftover 10.0 system-table incompatibilities
Bootstrapped node1 with galera_new_cluster, then started mariadb on node2 and node3 which joined the cluster via SST
Verified wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced/Primary state on all three nodes
Created a test table (galeratest.t1) and verified writes issued on node1, node2, and node3 each replicate to the other two members
Stopped mariadb on node2, confirmed the cluster stayed Primary/available at size 2, wrote new rows via node1 and node3 while node2 was down
Restarted node2, confirmed automatic resync: cluster_size back to 3, Synced, and all rows including those written during the outage present
Captured boot_id and cluster-health/data baselines on all three nodes

Restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling until each came back, confirming boot_id changed on each, and confirming each node returned to wsrep_cluster_size=3 / Synced / Primary with all 5 rows intact before restarting the next node
Final cross-node check confirming cluster_size=3, Synced state, and identical row set on node1 after all three restarts

evidence.requirement: Three-member Galera cluster formed, writes through any member visible from the others
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped (cluster_size=1), node2 and node3 joined (cluster_size=3, Synced on all). Writes made on node1, node2, node3 each appear on the other two members, confirmed by SELECT * on all three nodes showing the same 5 rows.

evidence.requirement: Cluster remains available/writable when one member is down; that member auto-resyncs on return
evidence.summary: node2 stopped; node1 and node3 still reported wsrep_cluster_size=2/Primary and accepted new writes (n1-down2, n3-down2). node2 restarted and automatically rejoined at cluster_size=3/Synced with both rows written during its downtime present, without manual intervention.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: baseline capture, one-at-a-time restart, boot-id proof, post-restart cluster/data recovery -- node1
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f41e1f8a...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then reachable again with boot_id fe1cb284... (changed); post-restart mariadb active, wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary, 5 rows intact.

Baseline boot_id e881ab3c...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then reachable with boot_id 42000c41... (changed); post-restart mariadb active, wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary, 5 rows intact.

Baseline boot_id 847a859d...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then reachable with boot_id 9030d7a1... (changed); post-restart mariadb active, wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, Primary, 5 rows intact.

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster consistency after all three restarts
evidence.summary: node1 post-all-restarts check: wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, and all 5 rows from throughout the exercise (including those written during the node2 outage) present and identical to earlier reads on node2/node3.
